question: A resistor has current flowing through it. If its resistance is halved while the voltage across it is kept constant, what will be the change in current?
solution:
The correct answer is __**It will be doubled.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current (I) flowing through a resistor is directly proportional to the voltage (V) across it and inversely proportional to the resistance (R). The formula is I = V/R.
 
• If the resistance (R) is halved and the voltage (V) remains constant, the current (I) will increase.
 
• Mathematically, if the initial resistance is R and it is halved to R/2, the new current will be I_new = V / (R/2) = 2V/R = 2I_initial.
 
• Therefore, halving the resistance while keeping the voltage constant will result in the current being doubled.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:**

 
 
• Formulated by Georg Simon Ohm in 1827.
 
• Defines the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in an electrical circuit.
 
• Expressed as V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
 
 
• **Resistance:**
 
 
• Measured in ohms (Ω).
 
• Determines how much a material opposes the flow of electric current.
 
• Factors affecting resistance include material, length, cross-sectional area, and temperature.
 
 
 
• **Current:**
 
 
• Measured in amperes (A).
 
• Represents the flow of electric charge in a circuit.
 
• Can be direct (DC) or alternating (AC).
 
 
 
• **Voltage:**
 
 
• Measured in volts (V).
 
• Represents the electrical potential difference between two points.
 
• Provides the driving force that pushes the current through the circuit.
